newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pfeiffer plans German listing to meet demand.
newsitem.headline: Pfeiffer plans German listing to meet demand.

text.p: Vacuum pump manufacturer Pfeiffer Vacuum Technology AG said on Thursday it planned to list its shares on the German stock exchange to meet strong home demand for its American Depositary Shares.
Chief executive Wolfgang Dondorf told a news conference the firm might consider raising its capital for the German issue.
Even now, a surprising 30 percent of Pfeiffer's existing shareholders were German, Dondorf noted.
The Asslar-based firm last year became the first ever German company to list its shares in New York before ever seeking a German listing.
Priced at issue at $11.50 when they opened in New York last July, Pfeiffer shares were up $0 5/8 at $22 at 1607 GMT.
Pfeiffer earlier reported a 175 percent surge in earnings per American Depositary Share (ADS) to 1.98 marks.
Dondorf added that Pfeiffer's sales rose 14.5 percent in the year to 249.5 million marks and should advance 10 percent this year.
However he said the firm would not pay a dividend for 1996 or 1997, but rather add its profits to reserves, since American investors were interested more in capital gains than dividend payments.
Formerly part of the diversified Swiss firm Oerlikon-Buehrle, Pfeiffer makes turbomolecular vacuum pumps, rotary vane pumps, root pumps, and customised vacuum systems.
Its sales are 27 percent German, 25 percent U.S. and 11 percent in the Far East.
